easy.prompt: A single artificial neuron (perceptron) computes its output by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Forming a weighted sum of inputs plus bias, then applying an activation function.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Sorting inputs and returning the median value.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Multiplying all inputs together without any bias term.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Counting how many inputs are nonzero, with no weights.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: y = σ(wᵀx + b) is the basic unit; depth stacks many such units with nonlinear σ.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Neurons use learned weights, not order statistics.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Affine transforms use sums and bias, not products alone.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That ignores continuous features and learned parameters.

easy.prompt: Stacking multiple hidden layers in a feedforward network primarily enables…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Guaranteed convex optimization of the loss.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Hierarchical feature composition through repeated nonlinear transforms.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Eliminating the need for any labeled data.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Fixed-size outputs regardless of input dimension.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Each layer builds increasingly abstract representations; depth adds expressive power beyond a single layer.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Deep nets are generally non-convex in their parameters.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Supervised deep learning still needs labels for training.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Architecture must match input/output shapes.

easy.prompt: During forward propagation in a feedforward network, each layer…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Updates weights using gradients from the next batch.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Transforms the previous layer's activations into new activations until the output layer.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Randomly permutes training labels.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Computes validation accuracy without using inputs.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Forward pass is inference through the computation graph: inputs flow toward predictions.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Weight updates happen after backward pass, not during forward.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Labels are fixed targets; forward pass uses features.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Predictions require passing inputs through the network.

easy.prompt: Backpropagation through a deep network applies the chain rule to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Propagate loss gradients backward through each layer's local Jacobians.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Cluster unlabeled examples into k groups.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Normalize pixel values to unit variance only at test time.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Select hyperparameters without computing any derivatives.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Reverse-mode autodiff multiplies ∂L/∂(layer output) by ∂(layer output)/∂(parameters) at each step.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Clustering is unsupervised; backprop computes supervised gradients.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Normalization is preprocessing, not gradient propagation.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Backprop explicitly computes derivatives for learning.

easy.prompt: Compared with a fully connected layer on images, convolution uses…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Fixed random filters that are never learned from data.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Local receptive fields and shared filters slid across spatial positions.

choices.label: C
choices.body: A separate unique weight for every input–output pair globally.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Only 1×1 kernels that never mix neighboring pixels.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Local connectivity and weight sharing exploit spatial structure and reduce parameters.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Conv filters are learned parameters.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That describes a dense layer on flattened pixels.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Typical conv kernels (3×3, 5×5) mix local neighborhoods.

easy.prompt: Stride greater than 1 in a convolutional layer…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Downsamples the spatial resolution of the feature map.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Increases channel depth without changing height or width.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Applies the same filter only once at the image center.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Removes the need for any activation function.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Stride s moves the kernel s pixels per step, producing smaller H×W outputs.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Channel depth is set by number of filters, not stride alone.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Conv slides across the input grid (subject to padding).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Activations remain important for nonlinearity.

easy.prompt: Zero-padding around an image before convolution is commonly used to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Control output spatial size (e.g., preserve dimensions with 'same' padding).

choices.label: B
choices.body: Guarantee that training loss is exactly zero.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Convert RGB images to grayscale automatically.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Replace backpropagation with a closed-form solution.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Padding adds border pixels so kernels can be applied at edges without shrinking excessively.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Padding affects geometry, not optimality of loss.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Channel reduction is a separate preprocessing choice.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Training still uses gradient-based learning.

easy.prompt: Max pooling over a 2×2 window with stride 2 typically…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Computes a weighted sum of all pixels in the image.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Halves height and width while keeping the strongest local response per region.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Applies a learnable 3×3 kernel at every position.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Doubles the number of input channels.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Max pool selects the maximum activation in each window, downsampling spatially.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That is closer to global average pooling over the whole map.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Pooling has no learnable weights (unlike conv).
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Pooling reduces spatial size; channel count is unchanged unless followed by conv.

easy.prompt: At each time step t, a vanilla RNN combines…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Independent parallel predictions with no shared parameters across time.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The current input x_t with the previous hidden state h_{t−1} to produce h_t.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The entire future sequence x_{t+1}, … before seeing x_t.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Only x_t, with no memory of earlier steps.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: h_t = f(W_h h_{t−1} + W_x x_t + b) recurs over time, carrying summarized history.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: RNNs share weights across time steps.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Causal RNNs do not use future inputs at step t.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That would be a feedforward model per step, not an RNN.

easy.prompt: Backpropagation through time (BPTT) on an RNN…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Propagates gradients only through the final time step.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Unrolls the recurrent computation over T steps and applies backprop on that graph.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Eliminates gradients by detaching all hidden states.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Trains each time step with a separate unrelated network.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: BPTT treats the unfolded chain as a deep feedforward net through time.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Earlier steps receive gradients via recurrent connections.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Detaching stops BPTT; standard training keeps the graph connected.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Shared weights tie steps together in one model.

easy.prompt: If the learning rate is far too large during SGD training, you often observe…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Gradients that are always exactly zero.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Instant convergence to zero loss in one iteration.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Oscillating or diverging loss instead of stable descent.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Automatic doubling of dataset size each epoch.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Oversized steps overshoot minima and can explode activations and weights.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That suggests vanishing gradients or a bug, not high LR alone.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Oversized steps rarely find a good minimum immediately.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Learning rate does not change the dataset.

easy.prompt: A mini-batch gradient update uses…

choices.label: A
choices.body: The exact full-dataset gradient every single step.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The average gradient over a subset of examples (batch size B).

choices.label: C
choices.body: One randomly chosen weight dimension per step only.

choices.label: D
choices.body: No stochasticity — only deterministic closed-form solves.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Mini-batches balance noise and throughput: ∇ ≈ (1/B) Σᵢ ∇ℓᵢ.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That is full-batch gradient descent.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: SGD updates use gradients for all parameters.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Mini-batch SGD is inherently stochastic.

easy.prompt: At inference time, dropout is typically handled by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Randomly zeroing half the neurons on every test example.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Doubling the learning rate for each layer.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Disabling dropout (or equivalently using the expected scaling used during training).

choices.label: D
choices.body: Removing all nonlinear activation functions.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Dropout is a training-time stochastic regularizer; the full network is used at test time.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That would inject noise into predictions at deployment.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Learning rate is not applied during inference.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Activations remain; only dropout masks stop.

easy.prompt: Data augmentation for images (random crops, flips) helps generalization by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Replacing the loss function with unsupervised clustering.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Guaranteeing that test images are identical to training images.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Exposing the model to plausible label-preserving variations during training.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Reducing the number of unique parameters to zero.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Augmentation simulates more diverse inputs without collecting new labels.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Augmentation keeps supervised labels on transformed inputs.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Test data should remain unseen; augmentation diversifies train only.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Augmentation does not remove parameters.

easy.prompt: Transfer learning in vision often starts by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Removing all convolutional layers and using only pooling.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Freezing the loss function so it never changes.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Using weights pretrained on a large dataset, then fine-tuning on the target task.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Training from random initialization only on three images.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Pretrained features (e.g., on ImageNet) provide strong low-level filters for new tasks.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Conv layers carry most transferable features.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: The loss is fixed by task; weights are what adapt.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Too little data; pretraining supplies useful representations.

easy.prompt: A flatten (reshape) layer before a classifier head…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Performs max pooling across the entire dataset.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Converts a convolutional feature map tensor into a 1D vector for dense layers.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Encodes positional information with sinusoids.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Applies a 3×3 convolution with stride 2.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: After conv blocks, H×W×C features are vectorized for fully connected classification.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Pooling operates on spatial maps, not batch-level flatten.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That describes transformer positional encodings.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Flatten does not convolve; it reshapes.

easy.prompt: Residual (skip) connections in ResNet add…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A second softmax over all hidden units.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Random noise sampled from the training labels.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The layer's input to its transformed output: y = F(x) + x.

choices.label: D
choices.body: The loss value directly to every weight matrix.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Identity shortcuts let gradients flow across blocks and ease optimization of very deep nets.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Softmax is typically an output activation, not a skip connection.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Skip connections add activations, not label noise.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Loss affects updates via gradients, not additive skip paths.

easy.prompt: One training iteration (step) usually means…

choices.label: A
choices.body: One random shuffle of the filesystem directory tree.

choices.label: B
choices.body: One parameter update from one mini-batch (forward + backward + optimizer step).

choices.label: C
choices.body: One evaluation pass over the test set only.

choices.label: D
choices.body: One complete pass through the entire training set.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Iteration counts optimizer steps; epoch counts full passes over the training data.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Shuffling data may happen, but an iteration is an update step.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Evaluation does not perform training updates.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That is one epoch, not one iteration.

easy.prompt: Weight decay in modern deep learning optimizers typically…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Replaces gradients with zero vectors.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Shrinks weights each step (often decoupled from the loss penalty in AdamW).

choices.label: C
choices.body: Randomly deletes entire layers each epoch.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Increases weight magnitudes to fight underfitting always.

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Decay adds a proportional shrinkage toward zero, improving generalization.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Gradients still drive learning; decay is an extra term.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That would be structural pruning, not weight decay.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Decay penalizes large weights; capacity is controlled elsewhere.

easy.prompt: An RGB image fed into the first conv layer is usually represented as a tensor with shape…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A single scalar brightness value only.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Sequence length × vocabulary size like text tokens.

choices.label: C
choices.body: 3 × 3 weight matrix shared across all datasets globally.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Height × Width × 3 channels (batch dimension added for mini-batches).

easy.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
easy.explanation: Color images have three channel maps (R, G, B) aligned spatially.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Images are spatial grids, not one number.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That is typical NLP input layout, not raw images.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: 3×3 may be kernel size; channels are separate feature maps.

medium.prompt: Stacking two 3×3 convolution layers (stride 1, same padding) yields an effective receptive field of…

choices.label: A
choices.body: 5×5 on the input (each 3×3 stack expands reach by 2 pixels per side).

choices.label: B
choices.body: 1×1 because kernels are small.

choices.label: C
choices.body: 3×3 only — depth does not increase receptive field.

choices.label: D
choices.body: 7×7 after one layer.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Receptive field grows with depth: two 3×3 layers see a 5×5 patch of the original grid.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Small kernels still aggregate context when stacked.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Each conv layer expands the region of input influencing an output.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Two 3×3 layers reach 5×5, not 7×7.

medium.prompt: A 1×1 convolution primarily…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Mixes channels at each spatial location without enlarging the receptive field.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Embeds word tokens into continuous vectors.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Convolves a large 7×7 neighborhood at every pixel.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Pools spatial dimensions by taking the maximum.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: 1×1 conv is channel-wise linear combination — useful for bottlenecks (e.g., Inception, ResNet).

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That is an embedding layer in NLP.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: 1×1 kernels do not look at spatial neighbors.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Pooling downsamples; 1×1 conv does not.

medium.prompt: Dilated (atrous) convolution increases receptive field by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Spacing kernel taps with gaps (dilation rate) without adding more parameters.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Using only 1×1 kernels exclusively.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Duplicating every filter across all datasets.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Removing nonlinear activations between layers.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Dilation r inserts r−1 zeros between kernel elements, expanding context per layer.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Dilation applies to larger kernels (e.g., 3×3 dilated).
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Dilation is an architectural spacing trick, not data copying.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Activations are independent of dilation.

medium.prompt: Batch normalization during training normalizes activations using…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Fixed constants set once before any training.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Gradients of the loss with respect to labels.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Statistics from the entire test set only.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Mean and variance computed over the current mini-batch (per channel).

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: BN uses batch statistics μ_B, σ_B then learns affine scale/shift γ, β.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Batch stats change each step.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: BN normalizes activations, not label gradients.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Test stats are not used for train-time normalization.

medium.prompt: Gradient clipping (by global norm) is used mainly to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Increase learning rate automatically every iteration.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Replace Adam with full-batch Newton steps.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Force all gradients to be exactly zero.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Cap the magnitude of the update when recurrent or deep nets risk exploding gradients.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: If ‖g‖ > τ, scale g ← τ·g/‖g‖ to prevent destabilizing parameter jumps.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Clipping bounds steps; LR schedules are separate.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Clipping is orthogonal to optimizer choice.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Clipping limits large gradients, it does not zero all learning.

medium.prompt: Cosine annealing of the learning rate…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Keeps η constant forever after the first step.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Doubles η whenever validation loss increases.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Sets every weight to zero at epoch 10.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Smoothly decreases η following a cosine curve over training epochs.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Cosine schedules decay LR toward a minimum, often helping late-stage fine convergence.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Annealing means η changes over time.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That is not the cosine schedule pattern.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: LR schedules adjust step size, not zero all weights.

medium.prompt: In an LSTM, the forget gate controls…

choices.label: A
choices.body: How much of the previous cell state c_{t−1} is retained versus erased.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Which optimizer (Adam vs SGD) is selected.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The RGB channel order of input images.

choices.label: D
choices.body: The number of layers in a ResNet backbone.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: f_t = σ(W_f·[h_{t−1}, x_t]) scales c_{t−1} before adding new content.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Gates are part of the RNN dynamics, not optimizer choice.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: LSTMs operate on sequences, not image channel layout.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That is CNN architecture design.

medium.prompt: A GRU compared with an LSTM…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Cannot model sequences longer than three steps.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Merges forget and input gating into update and reset gates with fewer parameters.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Uses only convolutional kernels over time.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Requires a separate cell state c_t distinct from h_t always.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: GRUs are a streamlined gated RNN often competitive with LSTMs on many tasks.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: GRUs handle long sequences (subject to training stability).
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: GRUs are recurrent, not purely convolutional over time.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: GRU combines state into hidden update without separate cell.

medium.prompt: Teacher forcing during RNN training means…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Disabling backpropagation through time entirely.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Feeding ground-truth previous tokens as inputs instead of the model's own predictions.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Using only unlabeled data for the loss.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Forcing the learning rate to zero after each epoch.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Teacher forcing speeds convergence but can cause exposure bias at inference.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: BPTT still runs; inputs are gold prefixes.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Seq2seq with teacher forcing is supervised on targets.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Teacher forcing concerns input feeding, not LR.

medium.prompt: A word embedding layer maps each token index to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A fixed 7×7 convolutional filter bank.

choices.label: B
choices.body: The probability of the next TCP packet.

choices.label: C
choices.body: A learned dense vector in ℝ^d used as input to downstream layers.

choices.label: D
choices.body: A one-hot vector of length equal to vocabulary with no learning.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Embeddings are lookup tables W[idx] trained end-to-end with the task loss.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Embeddings are for discrete tokens, not image filters.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That is networking, not NLP representations.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: One-hot is sparse baseline; embeddings are dense and learned.

medium.prompt: Label smoothing for classification replaces hard 0/1 targets with…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Soft targets (e.g., (1−ε) on the true class and ε spread over others).

choices.label: B
choices.body: All-zero targets for every class.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Random permutation of input pixels only.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Exact duplicate copies of the test set labels.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Smoothing discourages overconfident logits and can improve calibration.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Targets must remain a valid distribution.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That is image augmentation, not label smoothing.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Test labels must never leak into training targets.

medium.prompt: He (Kaiming) initialization is tailored for ReLU networks because it scales variance by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Using the global dataset mean as each weight.

choices.label: B
choices.body: fan-in (or fan-out for forward/backward balance) assuming half the activations are zeroed.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Initializing all biases to large positive values only.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Always setting every weight to exactly 1.0.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Var(w) ≈ 2/fan_in compensates for ReLU killing half the activations on average.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Init uses architectural fan-in, not data means.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Bias init is usually small/zero; variance scaling targets weights.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: He init samples from a distribution, not a constant.

medium.prompt: Depthwise separable convolution factorizes a standard conv into…

choices.label: A
choices.body: A fully connected layer on flattened pixels only.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Random Fourier features of the loss landscape.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Only average pooling with no learnable parameters.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Depthwise spatial conv per channel, then 1×1 pointwise mixing across channels.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Separable conv cuts compute (MobileNet) by decoupling spatial and channel mixing.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Separable conv keeps spatial structure.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That is unrelated to separable conv factorization.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Separable conv still has learnable depthwise and pointwise ops.

medium.prompt: Transposed convolution (often called 'deconv') is used to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Remove all parameters from the network.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Compute exact matrix inverse of the weight matrix.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Apply max pooling with stride 2.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Upsample feature maps (learned upsampling), e.g., in decoders and segmentation heads.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Transposed conv inserts stride gaps then convolves, increasing spatial resolution.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Transposed conv layers have learnable kernels.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: It is not a literal matrix inverse operation.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Pooling downsamples; transposed conv upsamples.

medium.prompt: An Inception module's parallel branches primarily allow…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Eliminating all parameters via weight sharing with labels.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Multiple filter sizes and pooling paths to be computed and concatenated in one block.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Training without any nonlinear activation.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Only a single 11×11 kernel with no alternatives.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Inception captures multi-scale patterns by fusing 1×1, 3×3, 5×5, and pool outputs.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Inception still has learnable filters per branch.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Activations remain inside branches.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Inception is defined by parallel multi-branch paths.

medium.prompt: VGG-style networks deepen using…

choices.label: A
choices.body: No pooling or striding anywhere.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Hand-crafted Sobel edge filters frozen forever.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Only 1×1 kernels with no spatial mixing.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Repeated stacks of small 3×3 convolutions instead of very large kernels.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Many 3×3 layers build large receptive fields with fewer parameters per layer than one huge kernel.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: VGG uses pooling between blocks.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: VGG learns filters end-to-end.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: VGG famously stacks 3×3 convs.

medium.prompt: Scaled dot-product attention computes weights as…

choices.label: A
choices.body: softmax(QKᵀ / √d_k) applied to V.

choices.label: B
choices.body: sigmoid(Wx + b) on raw pixels only.

choices.label: C
choices.body: k-means cluster assignments of batch norms.

choices.label: D
choices.body: The determinant of the Hessian matrix.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Attention distributes a convex combination of values based on query–key similarity.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: That describes a perceptron, not attention.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Clustering is unrelated to QKV attention.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Second-order determinants are not attention scores.

medium.prompt: A bidirectional RNN for sequence labeling…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Runs a forward and backward RNN and concatenates (or merges) their hidden states per step.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Cannot be applied to variable-length sequences.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Requires replacing all gates with 1×1 convolutions only.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Uses future labels at train time by leaking test answers.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Bidirection gives each position context from both past and future inputs.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: BiRNNs handle variable length with padding/masking.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: BiRNNs are recurrent, not purely 1×1 conv.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: It uses future inputs, not future labels, at position t.

medium.prompt: Adam's bias correction for the first moments exists because…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Gradients are always zero in deep nets.

choices.label: B
choices.body: m_t and v_t are initialized at zero, so early estimates are biased toward zero.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The learning rate must be infinite at step 1.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Batch normalization removes all stochasticity.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Corrected m̂_t = m_t/(1−β₁^t) (and similarly for v) fixes cold-start underestimation.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Adam assumes nonzero gradients on real tasks.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Bias correction stabilizes early steps, not infinite η.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: BN and Adam address different issues.

medium.prompt: Mixup training regularizes by…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Linearly interpolating pairs of inputs and labels: x̃ = λx_i + (1−λ)x_j, ỹ = λy_i + (1−λ)y_j.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Setting all weights to the same constant each step.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Removing nonlinearities from every layer.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Duplicating the test set into the training folder.

medium.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
medium.explanation: Mixup encourages linear behavior between examples and smoother decision boundaries.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Mixup blends examples, it does not collapse weights.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Mixup keeps standard architectures.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That would leak evaluation data.

hard.prompt: Reverse-mode autodiff (backprop) is especially efficient for neural nets when…

choices.label: A
choices.body: The loss is constant for all parameters.

choices.label: B
choices.body: No chain rule applies because activations are linear only.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Many inputs (parameters) influence few scalar outputs (loss), because one backward pass yields all ∂L/∂w.

choices.label: D
choices.body: There is only one scalar parameter and millions of outputs.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Reverse mode costs O(1) backward pass relative to forward for scalar loss — ideal for weight gradients.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Constant loss gives zero gradients — nothing to propagate.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Linear stacks still use chain rule; depth without nonlinearity collapses layers.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: That favors forward mode, not reverse mode.

hard.prompt: Truncated BPTT (TBPTT) trades off…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Exact full-history gradients with zero memory.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Elimination of all recurrent connections.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Faithful long-range gradient flow for lower memory by backpropagating only through K unrolled steps.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Guaranteed convexity of the RNN loss in all parameters.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: TBPTT cuts the unfolded graph every K steps, approximating long-term credit assignment.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Full BPTT over T steps costs O(T) memory; TBPTT approximates.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Recurrence remains; only backward horizon is shortened.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: RNN training remains non-convex.

hard.prompt: At inference, batch normalization uses running mean/variance because…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Dropout masks must be recomputed from test labels.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Mini-batch statistics would be noisy or undefined for batch size 1 and must match training scale.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Convolutions cannot run without batch size 32.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Gradients are not defined during inference.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Exponential moving averages of μ, σ collected during training stabilize normalization at test time.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Dropout is off at inference; unrelated to BN stats.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Conv works with any batch size; BN needs consistent stats.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Inference disables grad; BN still needs stable μ, σ.

hard.prompt: Layer normalization differs from batch normalization in that layer norm…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Can only be applied to the output softmax.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Requires batch size greater than 1000 always.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Uses test-set labels to compute variance.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Normalizes across features within each example (and time step), not across the batch dimension.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Layer norm is batch-independent — preferred in transformers and variable batch RNNs.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Layer norm is used inside blocks, not only at softmax.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Layer norm works with batch size 1.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Norm uses activations, never labels.

hard.prompt: Sharpness-aware minimization (SAM) seeks parameters that…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Maximize training loss on purpose.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Have zero gradient norm everywhere exactly.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Lie in flat regions of the loss landscape (robust to small perturbations), not just low loss points.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Eliminate the need for any validation data.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: SAM approximates worst-case loss in a neighborhood, favoring wider minima linked to generalization.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: SAM still minimizes loss, but penalizes sharp minima.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: SAM perturbs weights; gradients are generally nonzero.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: SAM is a training objective tweak; validation remains useful.

hard.prompt: Mode collapse in GAN training refers to…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Using only L2 loss on RGB pixels with no adversary.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Both networks sharing identical weights permanently.

choices.label: C
choices.body: The discriminator always outputting exactly 0.5.

choices.label: D
choices.body: The generator producing a small variety of outputs that fool the discriminator but lack diversity.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Collapsed generators map many z to few modes, failing to cover the data distribution.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: That describes pixel regression, not GAN collapse.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: GANs have separate G and D parameters.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Collapse is about limited support in generated samples.

hard.prompt: InfoNCE / contrastive learning objectives encourage…

choices.label: A
choices.body: All embeddings to become identical vectors.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Labels to be removed from self-supervised pipelines entirely without pairs.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Only k-means cluster centroids with no neural network.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Representations where augmented views of the same instance align and other instances repel.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Contrastive losses maximize agreement between positives and separate negatives in embedding space.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Collapse to a point is failure; contrastive losses prevent trivial solutions.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: Self-supervised still defines positive pairs (augmentations).
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: Contrastive SSL trains encoders with neural nets.

hard.prompt: For ReLU activations, the subgradient used in backprop is…

choices.label: A
choices.body: 1 where the pre-activation was positive and 0 where it was non-positive (convention at 0).

choices.label: B
choices.body: Always the second derivative of sigmoid.

choices.label: C
choices.body: Equal to the input x squared for all regions.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Undefined everywhere so gradients cannot flow.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: ReLU's gate multiplies upstream gradients by an indicator of active units.

wrongAnswerExplanations.b: ReLU backprop uses piecewise constant subgradient, not sigmoid derivatives.
wrongAnswerExplanations.c: That is not the ReLU derivative.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Subgradients at 0 are conventionally chosen; learning proceeds.

hard.prompt: When input and output dimensions differ in a ResNet block, the skip connection often uses…

choices.label: A
choices.body: Max pooling on the residual path only.

choices.label: B
choices.body: No skip at all — the block cannot be residual.

choices.label: C
choices.body: A learned 1×1 convolution (projection) to match channel/spatial size before the addition.

choices.label: D
choices.body: Softmax over all pixels in the skip branch.

hard.hint: Think about the precise definition before picking.
hard.explanation: Projection shortcuts align F(x) and x so y = F(x) + W_s x is well-defined.

wrongAnswerExplanations.a: Pooling changes resolution; 1×1 conv is the standard channel matcher.
wrongAnswerExplanations.b: ResNet uses projections instead of dropping skips.
wrongAnswerExplanations.d: Softmax is not used to align residual tensor shapes.

hard.prompt: The LSTM cell state's additive update c_t = f⊙c_{t−1} + i⊙g helps gradients because…

choices.label: A
choices.body: It forces every gate to be exactly zero always.

choices.label: B
choices.body: Gradients can flow across many time steps via near-identity paths without repeated Jacobian products shrinking to zero.

choices.label: C
choices.body: It removes all nonlinear gates from the network.

choices.label: D
choices.body: It replaces recurrence with a single feedforward layer.

hard.explanation: Additive memory provides a 'highway' mitigating vanishing gradients in long sequences.

hard.prompt: Multi-head self-attention splits Q, K, V into h heads primarily to…

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

choices.label: C
choices.body: Eliminate the need for any feedforward sublayers.

choices.label: D

hard.prompt: Sinusoidal positional encodings in the original Transformer…

choices.label: A

choices.label: B

choices.label: D

hard.prompt: AdamW decouples weight decay from the adaptive gradient step by…

choices.label: A

hard.prompt: The lottery ticket hypothesis suggests that…

choices.label: A

choices.label: B
